findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant factories
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an extension interface, but getShortcut() is added as an abstract method with no default implementation. Every existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory will fail to compile, and already-deployed implementations will throw AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() iterates all factories and calls getShortcut(). Token issuance/server startup can therefore break on upgrade; the method should have a default (e.g. unknown/na) implementation.

findings.title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context was removed
findings.body: The previously public Context(Context) copy constructor is deleted in this change. Code (including custom grant types/token-exchange code) that copied a grant Context will fail to compile and deployed binaries will fail with NoSuchMethodError. No replacement/deprecation is provided, so this is an unnecessary breaking API change in server-spi-private.

findings.title: Token issuance now fails for any grant type without a registered shortcut
findings.body: encodeTokenId() throws IllegalStateException when factory.getShortcutByGrantType() returns null, and TokenManager.initToken() now calls this for every access token. Previously a token could be issued for a grant/context whose grant_type string is not a registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory id (custom grants that call TokenManager directly, internal flows that set Constants.GRANT_TYPE themselves, or a grant factory returning no shortcut); now createClientAccessToken() aborts and no token is returned. Encoding context should fall back to the existing UNKNOWN ('na') shortcut instead of failing token issuance.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted and off-by-one grant check
findings.body: The encoded prefix is session(0-1)+tokenType(2-3)+grant(4-5), but the matcher checks substring(3,5) and returns false when that substring equals the expected grant shortcut. As written it rejects (partly) matching ids and accepts ids whose grant does not match, so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken no longer verify the grant type encoded in TOKEN_ID.

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: Line 73 repeats Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and encodeTokenId() silently produces an id ending in ':null' (which then decodes to the literal string "null"), corrupting the token id instead of failing fast at construction.
